messages:
zoe_support: Hey team — customer reports intermittent 401s and high tail latency. They said 'no request id in our server logs' and attached a single failing curl output. Can we give a short, copy-pasteable checklist so they can send a minimal repro (request id / trace / HAR / debug token)?

mike_sre: Yup — short checklist is best. I'll post a minimal curl they can run (captures headers) + Console & SDK locations. Keep it 3–4 steps they can do non-devs. :+1:

mike_sre: (1) Run this curl to reproduce and capture response headers — the request id will come back as a header named x-redwood-request-id (or X-Request-Id). Ask them to paste that whole header line.

```bash
curl -i -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  --write-out "\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}\n" \
  -o /tmp/response.txt
# then: grep -i x-redwood-request-id /tmp/response.txt || echo "no request id returned"
```

mike_sre: If they see a header like `x-redwood-request-id: 01F2ABCD1234`, that is the primary thing we need. If the header is missing, ask them to attach the full /tmp/response.txt file.

mike_sre: (2) Browser HAR (for web apps): In Chrome/Edge -> DevTools (F12) -> Network -> reproduce -> right-click -> Save all as HAR with content. Tell them to name the file and DM it to support. HAR should contain the outbound request and any 401 response.

emily_mobile: For mobile SDKs (iOS/Android) — quick steps for them to pull the session snippet: turn on debug logging for 30s, reproduce, and paste the last 50 log lines that contain `request_id=` or `req_ref=`. Example log line we look for: `I/Redwood: request_id=01F2ABCD1234 path=/v1/generate latency=217ms status=401`. If they can't access logs, tell them to open Settings -> App Debug -> Enable Redwood verbose and then repeat the request.

eng_oncall: (3) Debug token from Console (best if they can’t share logs): Console -> Projects -> Select Project -> Troubleshooting -> Create debug token. Set expiry 10m, copy token string and paste it into the support DM. We can use that token to fetch the internal request trace. If they prefer CLI, they can use `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEBUG_TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/debug/trace/<reqid>` (we'll provide endpoint after we have the req id).

mike_sre: (4) If they can run a proxied request, suggest this curl which records low-level TLS/HTTP details with --verbose and --trace-ascii: 

```bash
curl -v --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "small test"}'
# then attach /tmp/trace.txt (redact secrets)
```

mike_sre: Redaction note: they must redact API keys before sharing traces. They can keep request ids — those are safe and necessary.

zoe_support: I'll send that checklist to the customer now. Short note for them to include in the DM: one reproduced curl output (headers + body), the x-redwood-request-id (or the response file), a HAR if from browser, or the mobile log snippet, and optionally a debug token from the Console if they can create one.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded for release/infra-hotfix (sha: a1b2c3) — no infra changes affecting header names.

emily_mobile: If they tell us their SDK version, add that to the DM. Older SDKs log `req_ref` instead of `request_id`. Also ask which region (us-east/us-west/eu) — routing can affect trace availability.

zoe_support: Nice. I'll also ask them to mark the reproduction time (local timestamp) and timezone so we can align logs if the debug token isn't available. Sending now. :wave:
